surface: The intl-date editor with `imeFastEdit` on, where the browser focus sits in the editor's input while a cell is only selected: arriving on a date cell, opening the editor, typing a date, and Enter committing it.

steps.note: The setup gives the fixture's grid dates and times to show (its own values are not dates). ArrowLeft selects the date cell, drawn as `06/10/2024`. With `imeFastEdit` the grid first focuses the cell, then moves the focus to the editor's hidden date input, so an IME can start composing. Required: the selected cell's value. NVDA and VoiceOver with Chromium read the cell and then the hidden input (NVDA `date edit. Month, spin button, 06`, VoiceOver `06 Month stepper`), so a user who only moves hears an editor's control on every date cell. Finding: VoiceOver with WebKit says nothing.

Enter opens the editor on that cell: the native date input the focus already sat in, now shown, holding 2024-06-10. Required: the control, in the reader's words. NVDA said `date edit` when the focus arrived, so here it reads only the segment, `Month, spin button`, a synonym. Finding: NVDA with Firefox says nothing, because the focus does not move.
Eight digits fill the segments of the input (01/01/2020) in Chromium and Firefox; WebKit's input does not move to the next segment (the date editor scenario says more). Nothing is required here.

Enter commits the date and moves the selection one row down (enterMoves), to the next row's date, drawn as `01/05/2024`. The grid has no column headers, so the second data row is row 2. Required: that cell's value and its row. Finding: no reader reads the cell; the focus stays in the input, and NVDA and VoiceOver read a segment of it (`Year, spin button, 2024`, `1 month stepper`), or nothing.

ArrowUp moves to the edited cell, drawn as `01/01/2020`. NVDA reads the cell, then the hidden input again. Finding: VoiceOver reads only the input's month segment (`01 Month stepper` with Chromium, `12 month stepper` with WebKit), never the cell, because the focus returns to the input before VoiceOver speaks.
